featured_reviews.name: kavita bekal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually write reviews when I truly like a place, but I felt the need to share this experience because my stomach was upset after eating here, which is concerning.

I visited this restaurant expecting authentic Ratnagiri/Konkan food, especially given the name and the 4-star rating. Unfortunately, the food did not meet those expectations at all.

I ordered a fish thali, but there was nothing about it that reflected true Konkan or Ratnagiri cuisine. The fish fry was bland, not properly marinated, and lacked basic flavor. I had to add salt, pepper, and lime myself just to make it edible. Authentic Konkan fish fry is known for its seasoning and marinade, which was completely missing here.

The fish curry was a simple onion-based gravy with no depth—no kokum, no tamarind, no spice, and not even the correct color of a traditional fish curry. The thali included bhakri, rice, fish fry, fish curry, sol curry, and a dry fish preparation. Except for the dry item, nothing tasted authentic or satisfying.

I also ordered chicken sukka, which is supposed to be dry and at least mildly spicy. What was served was more like a regular chicken curry with gravy, not dry at all, and completely lacking spice and flavor. It did not resemble chicken sukka in any way.

I had high expectations, but the food was nowhere near what one would expect from a place claiming to serve Ratnagiri or Konkan cuisine. This food does not represent Konkan food, not even remotely.

Overall, a very disappointing experience, and due to both the quality of the food and the health issue afterward, I would not recommend this restaurant.

Whenever I’m in a new city, I make it a point to explore its traditional flavors. In Mumbai, Malvani food is always on my list. Since I was staying near Malad West, I decided to try Surmai, a Malvani/Mangalorean restaurant.
We ordered quite a few dishes, and while there were some good ones, the experience was mixed overall. Unfortunately, the signature dishes were a letdown. The fish curry in the thali was bland, lacking any real flavor, and the fish itself seemed like old stock. The bangda/mackerel fry was also disappointing, with fish that tasted frozen and not fresh.
On the brighter side, the clam sukka and prawn rava fry were enjoyable and definitely stood out. The sol kadhi, however, was more about color than taste and lacked the authentic punch.
I wish the restaurant paid more attention to freshness and flavor, especially in their star dishes, because Malvani food deserves much better representation.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited the newly renovated Shree Laxmi Vilas Bar in Malad East, and while there are a few things to appreciate, the overall experience ended up being a mixed bag — definitely not beyond 3 stars.

To begin with the positives, the renovation is genuinely impressive. The place looks fresh, modern, and much more inviting compared to most local bars in the area. The interior design is clean, well-lit, and thoughtfully done. The seating layout is comfortable and the ambience gives the feeling of a higher-end local bar. Even the crowd seemed more decent and composed than what you would typically expect in similar neighbourhood bars. This immediately makes the place feel safer and more comfortable, especially if you’re coming with friends.

However, the experience fell apart when it came to service and food, which are two of the most important aspects of any bar or restaurant. The waiter was completely inattentive — barely making eye contact, not checking on the table, and showing no interest in assisting with the order. When we pointed out issues, there was hardly any response.

The worst part was the Chicken Lollipop we ordered. The outer coating was extremely hard — so hard that it was difficult to bite into — but the waiter didn’t seem bothered at all. There was no attempt to replace it, apologise, or even acknowledge the complaint. It felt like the staff was simply not trained or not interested in customer satisfaction. The rest of the food was mediocre at best, definitely not worth the price they charge. For the kind of rates we paid, the quality should have been far better. It felt more like regular bar food but priced as premium.

They do have a smoking room, which is appreciated, but it clearly doesn’t match the new interiors. It looks old, under-maintained, and completely out of sync with the renovated main area. If they’ve taken the effort to upgrade the interior, the smoking room should be improved to the same standard.

Overall, Shree Laxmi Vilas Bar has potential — good ambience, good crowd, and a newly upgraded environment — but the poor service and disappointing food really pull the entire experience down. A place with such nice interiors should ideally offer much better hospitality. For now, it remains an average experience at best.

Tucked away in the greens of Aarey Colony, Hoy Maharaja Dhaba carries a rustic, countryside charm and gained quite a bit of attention through Instagram reels a few months ago.

The ambience leans into a traditional Maharashtrian dhaba vibe, with both outdoor and indoor (AC seating). We opted for the outdoor section, which was fairly comfortable thanks to well-placed fans that kept the space airy.

For food, we tried the pomfret fry and prawn fry. Both were fresh and decently spiced, making for a satisfactory meal. However, the flavours lacked the depth and authenticity you’d typically associate with coastal regions like Kashid or Dapoli.

The soul curry was enjoyable and comforting, while the lemon soda and kokam sharbat were refreshing additions to the meal. The detailing from the cutlery box to the plates, tumblers, and even the salt and pepper dispensers-did add a nice traditional touch to the overall setting.

That said, while the concept and ambience are appealing, the overall experience felt average and slightly overhyped. A decent visit, but not particularly memorable.

featured_reviews.name: Jyothis Thaliath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place for lunch.  It’s a Marathi-style seafood speciality restaurant that promises authentic coastal flavours.

Ambience:
The outdoor dining area has a lovely rustic vibe, perfect for evenings or cooler days. However, during hot afternoons, it can get quite uncomfortable. There’s also an indoor, air-conditioned section, but the tables are tightly packed and the sofa type seating is bit aged and not very comfortable.

Food:
We tried two thalis — Mutton Thali and Surmai Thali.

The Mutton Thali was the highlight of our meal. The mutton chops were tender, perfectly spiced, and among the best I’ve had in a while. The gravy was rich and flavourful without being overpowering. The marrow-filled bone was a pleasant surprise.

The Surmai Thali, on the other hand, was average. The fish fry portion was large but just okay in taste.

I wouldn’t recommend the Thalis here overall as most of the side dishes were quite oily and didn’t match my palate (though Maharashtrians might enjoy that style).

Thalis are priced on the higher side (₹600–₹1200). While portions are generous enough to share, I’d suggest skipping the Thali and focusing on starters or individual seafood dishes for better value and taste.

We also tried Butter Garlic Prawns, which were disappointing. Also, the prawns added into Thali curries felt out of place. They could consider swapping a few prawn dishes for clams or calamari, which are common in  Malvani cuisine.

Overall:
Don't fall for the social media hype. It's good for a visit if you’re in Aarey and craving for seafood.
